findings.title: The additive cut-count conclusion of Lemma 2.7 is false under its super-regularity assumptions

locations.anchor: Block expectation retains (1 ± 6 alpha^0.99), followed by Bernstein inference
Cut count used to rule out bad event in Lemma 2.10
Parts (i)–(iii) of Lemma 3.10 deduced from Lemma 2.7

findings.claim: For fixed X' subset X and Y' subset Y, |M[X',Y']| = |B[X',Y']|/(rho*n) ± n^0.8 with high probability.
findings.construction: Choose integer q arbitrarily large, alpha=1/q, d=1/2, and n an arbitrarily large multiple of 2q with n>(4q-2)^5. Put m=n/2,k=n/(2q), split X=X+ disjoint union X- into halves a_i,b_i, and let Y={y_0,...,y_(n-1)}. Delete b_i y_j from K_n,n exactly when (j-i) mod m is in {0,...,k-1}. Set Z empty.
findings.hypotheses: Degrees on X+,X-,Y are n,n-2k,n-k, respectively; rho=1-k/n>=1/2. Largest relative deviation is k/(n-k)=1/(2q-1)<=alpha. The deleted graph H has nk edges; for any S,T, eB(S,T)-rho|S||T|=(k/n)|S||T|-eH(S,T), whose absolute value is <=nk=alpha*n^2/2. Delta(Z)=0<n^0.4. An explicit perfect matching sends b_i to y_((i+k) mod m) and a_i to y_(m+i). Taking q first and then n respects n^-1 << alpha << d.
findings.decisive_evidence: For X'=X+ and Y'=Y every perfect matching has n/2 edges in the cut, whereas the asserted center is n/(2rho). Their difference is n/(4q-2)>n^0.8. The asserted event has probability zero for every matching distribution.
findings.independent_calculation: counterexample_check.py uses exact SymPy identities and integer/rational arithmetic; q=1000,n=4000^10 is an implicit large instance. An n=8,q=2 exhaustive-cut check is separately labelled structural diagnostic, not the asymptotic witness.
counterevidence_considered: Source-page image confirms the n^0.8 exponent and subset-equality notation.
Sets are fixed before the random matching, so no simultaneous-over-all-cuts interpretation is required.
Removing one Y vertex only changes the discrepancy by a bounded amount.
Approximate uniform edge marginals with fixed relative tolerance are compatible with the construction.
This is not a quasirandom host counterexample to Theorem 1.1.
findings.impact: A false guarantee in the principal Match subroutine is explicitly invoked in Lemmas 2.10 and 3.10. This damages a core proof justification, independently of whether the theorem survives a corrected error budget.
findings.repair_limits: A correction must include the degree-imbalance bias or impose stronger hypotheses, then propagate the new error through actual downstream uses. No complete repaired matching lemma or full downstream proof is certified.

independent_verification.evidence_positions: Publisher PDF pp.20–22 / printed1788–1790; dependencies PDF13,24–25,39–40.
independent_verification.conditions: Integer q is chosen first and arbitrarily large; alpha=1/q,d=1/2; n is a sufficiently large multiple of 2q satisfying n>(4q-2)^5. This respects n^-1 << alpha << d. X and Y each have n vertices; Z is empty.
independent_verification.decisive_independent_check: For m=n/2,k=n/(2q), each low-degree row loses 2k edges and each column loses k. Thus rho=(n-k)/n and relative degree error k/(n-k)=1/(2q-1)<=alpha. For every cut S,T the discrepancy equals (k/n)|S||T|-eH(S,T); both terms lie between 0 and nk, proving the required bound (indeed alpha*n^2/2). The proposed offset permutation is an allowed bijective perfect matching since k<m. For fixed X+=half of X,Y'=Y, every perfect matching has exactly n/2 cut edges; the stated center is n/(2rho), differing by n/(4q-2)>n^(4/5). Hence the alleged high-probability event is empty for every distribution, not merely unlikely.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Approximate marginals tolerate a linear bias and do not rescue the additive estimate. The cut is fixed, not chosen after M. Subset-equality is visible. With one Y vertex removed the discrepancy changes by at most 1+1/rho, so proper-subset readings also fail for sufficiently large n. The main tree-decomposition theorem is not refuted.
independent_verification.impact: The false guarantee is an explicit input to MATCH and the high-degree/approximate-decomposition arguments. Major is supported by a demonstrated core-related proof defect; it does not depend on establishing that the main theorem is false or that repair is difficult.
independent_verification.repair_boundary: No complete replacement lemma or downstream error propagation was verified. Degree-sensitive centering or an allowed regularity-dependent bias would require a new proof and checks of the cited applications.

independent_acceptance.result: Confirmed for the exact publisher PDF; Major retained. One inaccurate evidence-image annotation corrected; report TeX/PDF unchanged.
independent_acceptance.scope: Independent check of the single reported Problem: Theorem 1.1's quantifier boundary; the exact regularity definitions; every Lemma 2.7 hypothesis; the complete deterministic counterexample; the expectation/concentration mismatch; and actual uses in Lemmas 2.10 and 3.10. No new unrelated issue or whole-paper correctness claim.

independent_analytic_reasoning: Independently rederived all degrees, density, the uniform cut bound and perfect-matching construction, then compared the exact deterministic count to the asserted center.
Independently checked the quantified family, including that q is fixed before n and that n>(4q-2)^5 is equivalent to n/(4q-2)>n^0.8.
For the stored implicit instance q=1000,n=4000^10, the ratio discrepancy/tolerance is exactly 8000000/1999>1. The huge graph need not be materialized.

prior_calculations.method: Full script and stored exact output read and hash-bound; not re-executed in this acceptance. The analytic proof was independently rederived.

limitations: Focused independent acceptance of the reported claim, not a formal certification or complete reproof of all 58 source pages.
Theorem 1.1 and the specialized downstream conclusions have not been disproved; the established failure is the general cut-count lemma and its proof justification.
No verified complete repair or author adoption; no human adjudication.
The acquired arXiv v1 remains a separate source version; no equivalence to the publisher PDF is asserted.
